headline: Pilbara Minerals crashes 8% today as lithium selloff deepens — Middle East tension spikes oil above $103 and keeps markets on edge heading into a big US earnings week.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara dropped 8% today in a rough session for lithium. The lithium spot price is under serious pressure — analysts are warning key support levels are at risk after a broad selloff across battery metals. The long-term bull case (EV demand, FY27 price recovery forecasts) is still intact, but the near-term pain is real.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two slipped about 2% in last night's US session with no major company-specific news. The broader NASDAQ was slightly soft, and sentiment around gaming stocks has been cautious. No fundamental change to the GTA VI thesis — this looks like general market drift.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: The AI ETF dipped 1.35% today on the ASX, tracking softness in big tech names like Alphabet. The broader AI theme remains strong but investor patience is being tested as markets wait to see concrete earnings payback from AI infrastructure spending.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: Emerging markets slipped just over 1% today. Rising oil prices and a firmer USD can weigh on emerging market economies — many are oil importers. No single country-specific trigger; general risk-off mood in global markets.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: Alphabet fell about 1% last night despite strong cloud numbers — Google Cloud revenue reportedly jumped 82%. Investors are focused on the pace of returns from massive AI spending, and the stock lagged as the market asked 'when does all this capex pay off?' Q3 earnings are imminent and will be the real test.

movers.name: DHHF (BetaShares Diversified)
movers.note: DHHF nudged down 0.4% today — essentially flat. As a broadly diversified ETF, it absorbed the mixed global session well. Nothing to worry about here.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS slipped 0.5% today on the ASX, reflecting last night's mild S&P 500 pullback. The US market was off slightly as investors positioned ahead of a big earnings and Fed week. Long-term story unchanged.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG was essentially flat today, down just 0.13%. Its broad diversification across Australian and global shares smoothed out today's choppy session nicely.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft was the standout in your portfolio last night, gaining 0.66% while the broader NASDAQ was flat to lower. Markets are warming up ahead of Microsoft's earnings on October 28 — Azure cloud growth and AI revenue will be the key numbers to watch.

watch_today.title: Pilbara Minerals (PLS.AX) — bruising 8% drop today
watch_today.detail: PLS closed at $2.62, down 8% in a single session, and is now down over 61% on your total investment. The lithium price selloff is the culprit — analysts are warning support levels are cracking. However, some forecasters are still calling for a 63% price recovery in FY27 driven by EV demand. For a long-term holder, the thesis is still alive, but this is painful and volatile territory. Hold — selling now locks in a big loss at the bottom of the cycle.

watch_today.title: GOOG — Q3 earnings coming up, stock under short-term pressure
watch_today.detail: Alphabet fell 1% last night and is one of your smaller holdings (up 3.2% overall). Q3 results are due imminently and early signs are strong — cloud revenue reportedly up 82%. The dip is about investor impatience with AI spending timelines, not a business problem. Hold and watch the earnings print.

watch_today.title: MSFT — earnings on October 28, one to watch closely
watch_today.detail: Microsoft ticked up 0.66% last night and is your strongest performer overall (+18.4%). Full Q3 earnings land October 28 — the market wants to see Azure cloud growth and whether $50B+ in AI capex is starting to translate into revenue. Your long-term hold here looks solid. No action needed, but watch Tuesday's report.

watch_today.title: Oil surges above $103 — inflation risk back on the table
watch_today.detail: Crude oil (WTI) jumped nearly 4% last night to US$103.27 a barrel, driven by escalating Middle East tensions — reports of a potential fresh Israeli-US strike on Iran are circulating. Higher oil lifts petrol prices and can feed into inflation, which complicates rate cut expectations. Watch this — if oil stays above $100, it's a headwind for equities broadly.

watch_today.title: TTWO — still in the red overall, no new catalysts
watch_today.detail: Take-Two dropped about 2% last night and sits 5.6% below your total invested cost. No company-specific news. The GTA VI release is the long-term bet here — nothing has changed that story. Sit tight.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — down 14.9% overall, AI regulation risk building
watch_today.detail: The Global X AI ETF slipped 1.35% today and is your second-worst performer by percentage loss. There's growing regulatory pressure on AI globally — US states are moving to regulate while federal rules lag, and Wall Street regulators are putting AI firms under scrutiny. This is a long-term theme ETF — short-term swings are normal. Hold unless your view on AI's long-term growth has changed.

world.summary: The Middle East is the biggest global story today — Iran and Israel-US tensions are escalating sharply, pushing oil above $103. Meanwhile, Trump's administration is making unprecedented moves to block a US Senate election result, and global economic forecasters are debating whether 2027 could bring another financial crisis.

stories.title: US and Israel warned against fresh strikes on Iran as intelligence memo flags Iranian retaliation plots
stories.why_it_matters: Multiple outlets are reporting that the US and Israel are being warned not to launch another military strike on Iran, as the region sits on a knife-edge. A US intelligence memo has separately warned that Iran is plotting to kill Americans in the Middle East in retaliation for previous strikes. Oil jumped nearly 4% last night to over $103 a barrel on these fears — higher oil means higher petrol prices here in Australia and adds to global inflation pressure. Saudi Arabia has also postponed a major UN forum until 2027 citing regional tensions, a sign of how serious the situation is.

stories.title: Trump administration sues to block Alaska Senate election result if Democrat wins
stories.why_it_matters: The Trump administration has filed a lawsuit to block Alaska's US Senate election result before it's even been called — specifically targeting a scenario where Democrat Mary Peltola wins. Alaska uses a ranked-choice voting system and the result is still being counted. Legal experts say it's highly unusual and constitutionally questionable for the executive branch to try to block a state election outcome this way. Democrats are watching closely as they build a plan to dismantle Trump's agenda if they retake Congress.

stories.title: Immigrants seeking US citizenship targeted in illegal voting crackdown
stories.why_it_matters: The Trump administration is targeting immigrants who are in the process of becoming US citizens as part of a crackdown on illegal voting. Officials are scrutinising naturalisation applicants and cross-referencing voter rolls, a move critics say is designed to suppress legal immigrant voting. Civil rights groups argue it's creating fear among lawful residents going through the citizenship process. This is part of a broader pattern of the administration using executive power to shape electoral outcomes.

stories.title: Global Economic Outlook 2027: Are we heading toward another financial crisis?
stories.why_it_matters: Economic forecasters are sounding alarm bells about 2027, pointing to a combination of factors: high global debt levels, sticky inflation, elevated interest rates, and geopolitical disruptions to trade. The concern isn't an immediate crash but a slow squeeze — the kind that erodes asset values and consumer confidence over time. For Australian investors, this is a reminder that diversification across asset classes matters, and why broad ETFs like VDHG and DHHF are doing the job they're supposed to.

stories.title: World's fastest-growing economies in 2026 — India and emerging Asia lead the pack
stories.why_it_matters: The world's fastest-growing economies in 2026 are overwhelmingly in emerging Asia — India, Vietnam, and parts of Southeast Asia are leading global GDP growth rankings. This is directly relevant if you hold VGE.AX (Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF), which has exposure to many of these high-growth economies. While the ETF is down short-term, the long-run tailwind from emerging market growth remains a key part of the investment thesis.

markets.summary: The ASX barely moved today — up just 2 points to 8,795. US markets last night were mildly soft, with the S&P 500 down 0.5% and the NASDAQ off 0.2%. The big mover was oil, which jumped nearly 4% to US$103 on Middle East fears. Gold pulled back 1.3% after recent strong gains. The Aussie dollar edged up slightly to 70.4 US cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Essentially flat today — the local market held its ground despite offshore uncertainty.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night's US session was mildly negative, with investors cautious ahead of a big earnings and Fed week.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Tech was slightly softer last night — Alphabet weighed while Microsoft provided some offset.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Big jump on Middle East escalation fears — a potential Israeli-US strike on Iran has traders worried about supply disruptions.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold pulled back after recent record highs, but remains elevated as a safe haven play.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar ticked up slightly — holding just above 70 US cents.

politics.summary: No major Australian domestic political stories broke today. The news feed for Australian politics came back empty — it appears to have been a quieter day on the Canberra front.

stories.title: No major Australian political stories today
stories.why_it_matters: The Australian politics feed returned no stories today. Keep an eye on the RBA's next meeting and any federal budget update announcements, which are likely to be the next big domestic market movers.

ai.summary: The big AI theme today is regulation — US states are moving to fill a vacuum left by slow federal action, Wall Street's regulator is putting AI firms on notice, and an Aussie survey shows parents and teachers are worried about AI in classrooms. On the tools side, a detailed 2026 ranking of ChatGPT vs Claude vs Gemini vs Grok is doing the rounds.

stories.title: US states move to rein in AI as federal rules lag behind
stories.why_it_matters: With no comprehensive federal AI law in place in the US, individual states are now writing their own rules — creating a patchwork of regulations that tech companies have to navigate state by state. US tech leaders are reportedly calling for unified federal rules, noting that China already has a national AI regulatory framework. For investors in AI-exposed stocks like GXAI.AX, fragmented regulation adds compliance costs and uncertainty, but it also signals that AI is now mainstream enough to demand serious governance.

stories.title: Wall Street regulator to scrutinise AI use in corporate examinations
stories.why_it_matters: The SEC (America's share market regulator) has announced it will focus its corporate compliance examinations on how firms are using AI and how they're managing private assets. This is the first time AI use itself becomes a regulatory focal point for listed companies. Practically, this means companies that are cutting corners on AI disclosure or using AI in ways that could mislead investors are in the firing line. Good news for well-run companies; potential pain for those who've been vague about their AI strategies.

stories.title: Aussies worried about AI in classrooms — 'a reckoning is coming'
stories.why_it_matters: A new Australian survey shows growing anxiety about AI's role in schools — parents and teachers fear students are using AI to cheat, are losing the ability to think independently, and that schools aren't equipped to manage the change. The phrase 'a reckoning is coming' is being used by educators who say policy is years behind the technology. This is a live debate in Australia right now, with no clear national framework for classroom AI use in place.

stories.title: ChatGPT vs Claude vs Gemini vs Grok: Who's winning the AI assistant race in 2026?
stories.why_it_matters: A comprehensive 2026 ranking of the four major AI assistants puts ChatGPT still holding the largest market share at around 56.4%, with Claude, Gemini (Google's AI), and Grok (Elon Musk's xAI) all competing hard. For holders of GOOG, this matters — Gemini is Google's main AI product and its ability to claw back market share from OpenAI is a key part of the Alphabet growth story. The race is genuinely tight in capability terms, but ChatGPT's brand lead remains substantial.

sport.summary: It's Rugby League World Cup time — Tonga delivered a statement 36-0 thrashing of Lebanon to set up a blockbuster semi against Samoa. The AFL world is mourning the sudden death of former Port Adelaide player Daniel Stewart, aged just 37. And Australian surfer Stephanie Gilmore is leading the national team into an Olympic qualifying event.

stories.title: Tonga demolish Lebanon 36-0 to set up Samoa semi-final showdown
stories.why_it_matters: Tonga were absolutely dominant, shutting Lebanon out 36-0 in what was described as one of the most impressive performances of the tournament so far. They'll now face Samoa in what shapes as a mouthwatering Pacific derby semi-final. Meanwhile, the Women's and Men's Round 2 late mail has also been released — check NRL.com for injury and team news before the weekend's matches.

stories.title: AFL in shock: Former Port Adelaide player Daniel Stewart dies suddenly at 37
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL community is in shock following the sudden death of former Port Adelaide player Daniel Stewart, who was just 37 years old. No cause of death has been publicly confirmed. Stewart played for Port Adelaide and the news has prompted an outpouring of tributes from players, clubs, and fans across the country. A reminder of how quickly life can change — our thoughts are with his family.

stories.title: Stephanie Gilmore leads star-studded Australian surfing team with Olympic places on the line
stories.why_it_matters: Seven-time world champion Stephanie Gilmore is headlining a strong Australian team heading into a crucial Olympic qualifying event. With Paris 2028 Olympic spots up for grabs, this is a high-stakes event for the squad. Australian sensation Molly Picklum is also in the mix, competing at the WSL Philippines Pro at Cloud 9, Siargao from October 30 to November 8 — one of the most iconic surf breaks in the world.

stories.title: Gold Coast Titans player Bai contract saga — should he honour his deal?
stories.why_it_matters: There's a local Gold Coast angle here — a debate is brewing about whether Titans player Bai should honour his existing contract or push for a move. SEN is reporting the story as part of the wider NRL off-season signings watch. No resolution yet, but Gold Coast fans will be watching closely given the Titans' rebuilding phase.
